correctness.rationale: The integer polynomial identity gives a Hessian circulant with factors (t-1)(t^a-1)(t^(a+1)+1); gcd(a,n)=1 makes the middle difference have image equal to the augmentation ideal. The exact sequence separates odd and even shift-cycle lengths. In the odd regime it identifies an elementary two-group extension of Z/n, whose splitting is determined by the rank mod two. In the even regime torsion embeds in Z/n, and the exact pseudodeterminant/primitive-kernel Gram ratio gives order n/2. All normalization, modulus, and parity hypotheses are stated. Exact Smith computations verified 154 finite samples but are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The Euler form is a canonical invariant of cyclic quotient surface stacks studied in a current algebraic-geometric classification. The theorem classifies the entire integral cokernel, not merely its rank or sampled numerical values, for all isolated cyclic actions with two faithful coordinate characters. It gives a sharp jump in free rank controlled by the parity of n/gcd(n,a+1), and a dichotomy between elementary two-torsion plus one large cyclic factor and purely cyclic torsion. These are natural structural data of the underlying representation lattice and go beyond previously computed special-weight cases; the result is not offered as a Hilbert-scheme existence or enumerative theorem.
